Action Plan:
1. Prescribe topical steroid cream for inflamed, cracked palmar skin — prescription to be sent to the patient's pharmacy (topical steroid name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
2. Advise use of a stronger emollient applied to affected hands 3–4 times daily for the next couple of weeks.
3. Advise avoidance of triggers: wear protective gloves at all times when performing cleaning tasks/using cleaning products.
4. Provide expectation and safety-netting: expect improvement in ~10–14 days; if no improvement by 1–2 weeks or if condition worsens/spreads, patient to return sooner for review.
5. Document that the patient has been given the prescription and practical advice about application and glove use.
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: soreness, cracked skin and dryness of hands, mainly the palms; intermittent itchiness; pain affecting ability to work.
- Onset/duration/progression: symptoms began approximately 3–4 months ago; have gradually worsened and now cause significant pain and work impairment; patient has been off work for the past 3 days due to symptoms.
- Symptom features: cracking of skin; itching not constant; bleeding only after scratching (no spontaneous bleeding reported).
- Attempts at treatment: trialed E45 emollient (no benefit); tried an antihistamine (no benefit).
- Occupational history: hotel housekeeper; performs bedroom and bathroom cleaning; frequently uses bathroom cleaning products; not consistently wearing gloves; changed jobs 4 months ago.
- Systems review: denies fever, nausea, vomiting, bowel or urinary symptoms; appetite maintained.
- Past medical history: type 2 diabetes.
- Medications: metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: none reported.
- Social history: non-smoker; drinks a couple of pints of alcohol per week.

Objective:
- No clinician-recorded physical examination findings or vital signs documented in transcript.
- Patient-reported examination findings: cracked palmar skin, soreness, intermittent itch, occasional bleeding after scratching.
- No investigations recorded or performed during the consult.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Hand dermatitis (issue name only):
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Contact dermatitis.
   - Differential diagnosis: Irritant contact dermatitis; allergic contact dermatitis; atopic dermatitis (if applicable).
   - Investigations planned: None documented.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Topical steroid cream — prescription to be sent to pharmacy (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Stronger emollient — apply to affected hands 3–4 times daily for the next couple of weeks.
   - Relevant referrals: None documented.

2. Occupational exposure to cleaning products (issue name only):
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Occupational contact dermatitis.
   - Differential diagnosis: Not additionally specified.
   - Investigations planned: None documented.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Avoid triggers where possible; wear protective gloves at all times when cleaning.
   - Relevant referrals: None documented.

3. Type 2 diabetes (issue name only):
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Type 2 diabetes.
   - Differential diagnosis: Not applicable.
   - Investigations planned: None documented in this consult.
   - Treatment planned: Continue current medication (metformin — dose/route/frequency not documented).
   - Relevant referrals: None documented.

- Missing but clinically expected elements: clinician physical examination findings (skin exam, extent/severity), vital signs, specific topical steroid name and dosing instructions, specific emollient product name, documentation of sick note/work clearance if required, diabetes control data (recent HbA1c or blood glucose), and documentation of whether infection is suspected.
- Internal conflicts from transcript: none identified.
